text: A microbrewery, also called a craft brewery, is a brewery that produces small amounts of beer, or sometimes root beer, and is typically much smaller than large-scale corporate breweries.
Microbreweries are independently owned and are generally characterized by their emphasis on quality, flavour and brewing technique.
South Dakota is one of 14 U.S. states that forbids small breweries from directly distributing beer products.
Under South Dakota law, small breweries are required to use a distributor to sell their beer, and the article is a list of breweries in South Dakota.
Beer is the world's most widely consumed alcoholic beverage and is the third-most popular drink overall, after water and tea.
Beer is thought by some people to be the oldest fermented beverage, and the diversity of size in breweries is matched by the diversity of processes, degrees of automation and kinds of beer produced.
A brewery is a dedicated building for making beer, although beer can be made at home, as it has been for much of beer's history, and a company that makes beer is called a brewery or brewing company.
A brewery is typically divided into distinct sections, with each section reserved for one part of the brewing process.
A microbrewery is a brewery which produces a limited amount of beer, and the qualifications to be classified as a microbrewery vary by country.
The term microbrewery originated in the United Kingdom in the late 1970s to describe a new generation of small breweries focused on producing traditional cask ale.
The first successful example of this approach was Litchborough Brewery, founded by Bill Urquhart in 1975 in the Northamptonshire village of the same name.
The term microbrewery spread to the United States in the 1980s, where it came to designate breweries producing fewer than 15,000 U.S. beer barrels (1,800,000 liters or 475,000 U.S. gallons) annually.
Stone Brewing, headquartered in Escondido, California, USA, was founded in 1996 in San Marcos, California, and is the largest brewery in Southern California.
Based on 2016 sales volume, Stone Brewing is the ninth largest craft brewery in the United States.
Beer Wars is a 2009 documentary film about the American beer industry, and in particular about the differences between large corporate breweries and smaller craft breweries.

Beer Wars contrasts the large corporate breweries Anheuser-Busch, the Miller Brewing Company and the Coors Brewing Company with smaller producers such as Dogfish Head Brewery, Moonshot 69, Yuengling and Stone Brewing Co.
Beer Wars argues that advertising and lobbyists are used to control the beer market, implying that this harms competition and consumer choice.
The 2013-14 Iona Gaels men's basketball team represented Iona College during the 2013-14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season, led by fourth year head coach Tim Cluess.
The 2013-14 Iona Gaels played their home games at the Hynes Athletic Center and were members of the Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference (MAAC).
The 2013-14 Iona Gaels finished the season 22-11, 17-3 in MAAC play, to win the MAAC regular season championship, then lost the MAAC Tournament championship game to Manhattan.

As a regular season conference champion that failed to win its conference tournament, the 2013-14 Iona Gaels received an automatic bid to the National Invitation Tournament, where they lost in the first round to Louisiana Tech.
The 2012-13 Iona Gaels men's basketball team represented Iona College during the 2012-13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season under third year head coach Tim Cluess.
The 2012-13 Iona Gaels played home games at the Hynes Athletic Center, were members of the MAAC, and finished the season 20-14, 11-7 in MAAC play, tied for fourth place.

The 2012-13 Iona Gaels won the MAAC Tournament by defeating Manhattan in the championship game, earning an automatic bid to the 2013 NCAA Tournament, where they lost in the second round to Ohio State.

The 2015-16 Iona Gaels men's basketball team represented Iona College during the 2015-16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season under sixth year head coach Tim Cluess, playing home games at the Hynes Athletic Center.
The 2015-16 Iona Gaels finished the season 22-11 overall and 16-4 in MAAC play, to finish in second place in the Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference.

The 2015-16 Iona Gaels defeated Canisius, Siena and Monmouth to win the MAAC Tournament and the conference's automatic bid to the NCAA Tournament, where as a #13 seed they lost in the first round to Iowa State.
The 2015-16 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team represented Iowa State University during the 2015-16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season and competed in the Big 12 Conference.
The 2015-16 Iowa State Cyclones were coached by Steve Prohm, in his 1st season, and played their home games at Hilton Coliseum in Ames, Iowa.
David A. Hobbs, born April 25, 1949, is an American basketball coach who currently serves as a special assistant to Iowa State's head coach Steve Prohm.
David A. Hobbs was the men's head coach at the University of Alabama from 1992 to 1998 and was also an assistant coach at Alabama, the University of Kentucky and Virginia Commonwealth University.

The 2014-15 Iona Gaels men's basketball team represented Iona College during the 2014-15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season under fifth year head coach Tim Cluess, playing home games at the Hynes Athletic Center.
The 2014-15 Iona Gaels finished the season 26-9 overall and 17-3 in MAAC play, winning the MAAC regular season championship.

After defeating Siena and Monmouth, the 2014-15 Iona Gaels reached the MAAC Tournament championship game, where they lost to Manhattan; as a regular season champion that failed to win the tournament, they received an automatic bid to the National Invitation Tournament, losing in the first round to Rhode Island.

The 2011-12 Iona Gaels men's basketball team represented Iona College during the 2011-12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season under second year head coach Tim Cluess, playing home games at the Hynes Athletic Center.
The 2011-12 Iona Gaels were MAAC regular season champions but failed to win the MAAC Basketball Tournament, losing to Fairfield in the semifinals.

The 2011-12 Iona Gaels received an at-large bid to the 2012 NCAA Tournament, where they lost to BYU in the First Four round; the Gaels led BYU by 25 points in the second half, and the comeback was the largest in NCAA Tournament history.

The 2012-13 Murray State Racers men's basketball team represented Murray State University during the 2012-13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season under second year head coach Steve Prohm, playing home games at the CFSB Center.
The 2012-13 Murray State Racers, members of the West Division of the Ohio Valley Conference, finished 21-10 overall and 10-6 in OVC play to win the West Division title.
The 2012-13 Murray State Racers lost the OVC Tournament championship game to Belmont in overtime and, despite their 21 wins, did not participate in any postseason tournament.

The 2010-11 Iona Gaels men's basketball team represented Iona College during the 2010-11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season under first year head coach Tim Cluess, playing home games at Hynes Athletics Center.
The 2010-11 Iona Gaels finished the season 25-12, 13-5 in MAAC play, and lost the championship game of the 2011 MAAC Men's Basketball Tournament to Saint Peter's.
The 2010-11 Iona Gaels were invited to the 2011 CollegeInsider.com Tournament, where they advanced to the championship game before falling to Santa Clara.

The 2016-17 Iona Gaels men's basketball team represented Iona College during the 2016-17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season under seventh year head coach Tim Cluess, playing home games at the Hynes Athletic Center in New Rochelle, New York.
The 2016-17 Iona Gaels finished the season 22-13 overall and 12-8 in MAAC play, tying for third place in the conference.
The 2016-17 Iona Gaels defeated Rider, Saint Peter's and Siena to win the MAAC Tournament, earning the automatic bid to the NCAA Tournament, where they lost in the First Round to Oregon.
Grand Duke Vladimir Alexandrovich of Russia (22 April 1847 - 17 February 1909) was a son of Emperor Alexander II of Russia and a brother of Emperor Alexander III of Russia.
Grand Duke Vladimir Alexandrovich was the senior Grand Duke of the House of Romanov during the reign of his nephew, Emperor Nicholas II.
Grand Duke Sergei Alexandrovich of Russia (May 11, 1857 - February 17, 1905) was the fifth son and seventh child of Emperor Alexander II of Russia.
Grand Duke Sergei Alexandrovich was an influential figure during the reigns of his brother Emperor Alexander III of Russia and his nephew Emperor Nicholas II.
Grand Duke Sergei Alexandrovich was the brother-in-law of Emperor Nicholas II through his marriage to Elizabeth, the sister of Tsarina Alexandra.
Charles Sydney Gibbes (19 January 1876 - 24 March 1963) was a British academic who served as the English tutor to the children of Emperor Nicholas II of Russia from 1908 to 1917.
When Nicholas II abdicated the throne in March 1917, Charles Sydney Gibbes voluntarily accompanied the Imperial family into exile in the Siberian village of Tobolsk.

After the Imperial family was murdered in 1918, Charles Sydney Gibbes returned to the United Kingdom, became an Orthodox monk adopting the name Nicholas in commemoration of Nicholas II, and died in 1963, buried at Headington cemetery, Oxford.

The October Manifesto, officially The Manifesto on the Improvement of the State Order, was issued by Emperor Nicholas II on 30 October 1905 (O.S. 17 October), under the influence of Sergei Witte, as a response to the Russian Revolution of 1905.
The October Manifesto served as a precursor to the Russian Empire's first constitution, which was adopted the following year.
The October Manifesto promised basic civil rights and an elected parliament called the Duma, without whose approval no laws were to be enacted in Russia in the future.

Emperor Nicholas II strenuously resisted these ideas and gave in after Grand Duke Nicholas, his first choice to head a military dictatorship, threatened to shoot himself if the Tsar did not accept Witte's suggestion.

Russia-United Kingdom relations describe the relationship between the Russian Federation and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and its overseas territories, spanning nearly five centuries.
Russia and the United Kingdom were allies against Napoleon, enemies in the Crimean War of the 1850s, and rivals in the Great Game for control of central Asia in the late 19th century.

Russia and the United Kingdom were allies again in World Wars I and II, although relations were strained by the Russian Revolution of 1917, and they were at sword's point during the Cold War (1947-91).
Russian big businesses had strong connections with the City of London and British corporations during the late 1990s and 2000s.
Ural State Mining University is a university situated in Yekaterinburg, Russian Federation, and it was founded in 1914.
In 1917, Nicholas II signed an order placing the Yekaterinburg Institute of Mines under his patronage and giving the institution the title The Emperor Nicholas II Ural Institute of Mines.
Nicholas II (Nikolai II Aleksandrovich), born 18 May [O.S. 6 May] 1868 and died 17 July 1918, was the last Emperor of Russia, ruling from 1 November 1894 until his forced abdication on 15 March 1917.
During the reign of Nicholas II, the Russian Empire fell from being one of the foremost great powers of the world to economic and military collapse.

Due to the Khodynka Tragedy, anti-Semitic pogroms, Bloody Sunday, the violent suppression of the 1905 Revolution, the execution of political opponents and his perceived responsibility for the Russo-Japanese War, Nicholas II was nicknamed Nicholas the Bloody by his political adversaries.
Soviet historiography portrayed Nicholas II as a weak and incompetent leader whose decisions led to military defeats and the deaths of millions of his subjects.
Prince Andrew Andreyevich Romanov, born 21 January 1923, is a Russian American artist and author and a grand-nephew of Russia's last Emperor, Nicholas II.
Since December 31, 2016, Prince Andrew Andreyevich Romanov has been a claimant to the headship of the Imperial House of Russia and President of the Romanov Family Association.
Prince Andrew Andreyevich Romanov is a great-great-grandson in the male line of Emperor Nicholas I of Russia.
The Russian Revolution was a pair of revolutions in Russia in 1917 that dismantled the Tsarist autocracy and led to the rise of the Soviet Union.

The Russian Empire collapsed with the abdication of Emperor Nicholas II, and the old regime was replaced by a provisional government during the first revolution of February 1917 (March in the Gregorian calendar).

In the second revolution of October 1917, the Provisional Government was toppled and all power was given to the soviets, the grassroots community assemblies that had arisen alongside the provisional government.
Grand Duke Alexander Alexandrovich of Russia (7 June 1869 - 2 May 1870) was the infant son of Alexander III, the heir apparent styled Tsesarevich, and his consort Marie Fyodorovna of Russia.
Grand Duke Alexander Alexandrovich was the second child and second son of Alexander III and Marie Fyodorovna of Russia, and the younger brother of the future Emperor Nicholas II.

Grand Duke Alexander Alexandrovich died of meningitis in 1870, one month before his first birthday, and his mother Marie Fyodorovna wrote to Queen Louise of Denmark that the doctors maintained he did not suffer.
Castle Air Force Base is a former United States Air Force Strategic Air Command base located northeast of Atwater and northwest of Merced, about 115 miles (185 km) south of Sacramento, California.
Castle Air Force Base, which operated from 1941 to 1995, was a former Strategic Air Command base in California.
The Pacific Flying Club is a flight school based out of Boundary Bay Airport in Delta, British Columbia, and is the largest flight school on the west coast of Canada.
The Pacific Flying Club was formed on July 14, 1965, and planned to celebrate its 50th anniversary in 2015 by hosting the Webster Memorial Trophy Competition.

The North American Institute of Aviation (NAIA) was a private, FAA Part-141 flight school located in Conway, South Carolina, United States, operating out of the Conway-Horry County Airport, where it was also the fixed-base operator.
The North American Institute of Aviation was founded on July 7, 1972 in Hammonton, New Jersey, moved to South Carolina in 1978, and specialised in flight and aircraft maintenance training.

The North American Institute of Aviation had close connections to North European Aviation Resources (NEAR) of Vigra, Norway, was for a period the ab-initio school of Scandinavian Airlines, and also had a campus in Las Cruces, New Mexico.
Aerocondor (ATA Aerocondor Transportes Aereos Lda) was an airline and flight school based in Cascais, Portugal, operating scheduled regional services in mainland Portugal and to Madeira.

Aerocondor also operated scheduled passenger services in France and charter services to the United Kingdom and Spain, with its main bases at Portela Airport in Lisbon and Madeira Airport, and its own flight school at Cascais Aerodrome.

American Airlines Flight 157 was a civil aviation accident that resulted in 28 fatalities; the Douglas DC-6 was flying on November 29, 1949, from New York City to Mexico City with 46 passengers and crew.

After one engine of American Airlines Flight 157 failed in mid-flight, a series of critical mistakes by the flight crew caused the pilot to lose control during the final approach to a routine stopover at Love Field in Dallas, Texas.

American Airlines Flight 157 slid off the runway and struck a parked airplane, a hangar and a flight school before crashing into a business across from the airport; 26 passengers and two flight attendants died, while the pilot, co-pilot, flight engineer and 15 passengers survived.
American Flyers is an American flight school, founded at Midway Airport in 1939 by Reed Pigman, and is the oldest flight training school in the United States.

In 1980, the flight school chain Aviation Training Enterprises (A.T.E.) acquired American Flyers, which now operates nine locations across the United States providing flight training to domestic and international students.

American Flyers, previously based in West Chicago, Illinois, produces more instrument-rated pilots than any other school in the nation and is an FAA-approved part 141 school offering a 6 months program with a rigid training course syllabus and standardized instructors.
The Sierra Academy of Aeronautics is an aviation flight school headquartered in Atwater, California, and operates its training facility at the former Castle Air Force Base in Atwater.
The Sierra Academy of Aeronautics is contracted by several foreign air carriers to perform pilot training, including Shanghai Airlines.
Jeremiah Atwater (December 27, 1773 - July 29, 1858) was notable as an educator, minister and college president, and became the first president of Middlebury College.
Jeremiah Atwater became principal of the Addison County Grammar School in 1799 and, a year later, when the school became Middlebury College, assumed the role of its first president.

In 1809, Jeremiah Atwater left Middlebury to become the third president of Dickinson College in Pennsylvania, remaining until 1815, when he returned to New Haven, Connecticut, his birthplace and the home of his alma mater, Yale University.

Atwater Commons, one of five residential commons at Middlebury, is named for Jeremiah Atwater, Dickinson College has an Atwater Hall named for him, and he was elected a member of the American Antiquarian Society in 1815.
ATP Flight School, headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida, is the largest flight training company in the United States.
ATP Flight School is a privately held company founded in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1984 by its current management, a small group of airline pilots.

ATP's initial focus was flight training for U.S. military pilots seeking Airline Transport Pilot Certificates to transition to commercial air carrier operations; it later added ab-initio programs for domestic and international students and is today the leading supplier of professionally trained pilots to the nation's regional airlines.
Huffman Aviation was a flight-training school based in Venice, Florida, at Venice Municipal Airport, and it has no affiliation with a flight school in Texas with the same name.
The Huffman Aviation flight school in Venice, Florida, has no affiliation with a flight school in Texas that carries the same name.
FOB Shank, also known as Firebase Shank, is a forward operating base of the U.S. military, with IATA code OAA and ICAO code OASH.
FOB Shank is located in Logar province of Eastern Afghanistan, about 12 km south-east of the city of Baraki Barak.

The Kathiawar Agency was a political unit on the Kathiawar peninsula (Saurashtra) in the western part of the Indian subcontinent, covering about 23,445 square miles, that is now part of Gujarat state.
The Kathiawar Agency was made up of some 200 small princely states under the suzerainty of the Bombay Presidency of British India.

Within the Kathiawar Agency, about 1,245 square miles with 173,436 persons belonged to the Gaikwar, about 1,298 square miles with 128,559 persons to Ahmadabad District, and about 20 square miles with 14,614 persons to the Portuguese possession of Diu.
The vast remainder of the Kathiawar Agency, the territory forming the Political Agency, covered about 20,882 square miles with a population of 2,329,196 persons.
The Maseed (also spelled Mahsud or Masid) is a Karlani Pashtun tribe inhabiting parts of the South Waziristan Agency in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas of Pakistan.
Maseed lineages are settled in Logar Province of Afghanistan, especially in Charkh District, Baraki Barak and Muhammad Agha, and also in Wardak, Ghazni and Kunduz provinces.

The Maseeds inhabit the centre and north of the South Waziristan valley, surrounded on three sides by the Darweshkhel Wazirs and shut off on the east by the Bettanis, and the Ormur (Burki) tribe's stronghold of Kaniguram lies within Maseed territory.

The Ormurs are considered by other South Waziristan tribes to be close brethren of the Maseeds, due to marital and other ties, and have lived in and controlled Kaniguram for over a thousand years; some Maseeds also live in the UAE, Germany and the United Kingdom.
The Baraki Barak airstrike was a coalition airstrike that occurred on August 26, 2011, in Eastern Afghanistan.
In the Baraki Barak airstrike, six Afghan civilians from the same family were killed in the Baraki Barak district of Logar province, Afghanistan.
In the Baraki Barak airstrike, four insurgents and three Afghan army members were also killed.
Baraki Rajan is a town within the Baraki Barak District of Logar Province, Afghanistan, lying approximately 3 km south of Baraki Barak, the capital of the Baraki Barak District.

Baraki Rajan is the location of the largest bazaar in the Baraki Barak District, with over 1,200 shops and businesses, and a 50-plus bed hospital near the town centre, making it an important centre for commerce in the district.
Logar is one of the 34 provinces of Afghanistan, located in the eastern section of the country, and is divided into seven districts containing hundreds of villages.
The capital of Logar Province, one of the 34 provinces of Afghanistan, is Puli Alam.

Baraki Barak District is situated in the western part of Logar Province, Afghanistan, bordering Wardak Province to the west and northwest, Pul-i-Alam District to the north and east, and Kharwar and Charkh districts to the south.

Baraki Barak District had a population of 101,000 in 2006, and its district centre is the town of Baraki Barak, the former provincial capital, located in the northern part of the district in the valley of the Logar River.
Baraki Rajan, another important town in Baraki Barak District, lies 4 km from the district centre.
A camptown in Lesotho is the district capital of one of the ten districts of Lesotho, usually a commerce hub where the district's central government offices are located.

Camptowns usually take the same name as their district: the camptown for Maseru District is Maseru, the camptown for Thaba-Tseka District is Thaba-Tseka, and the largest camptown is the city of Maseru.
The exceptions are Berea District, whose camptown is Teyateyaneng, Quthing District, whose camptown is Moyeni, and Leribe District, whose camptown is most often called Hlotse.
Baraki Barak is a town and the centre of Baraki Barak District in Logar Province, Afghanistan, and was also the former capital of Logar Province.
The town of Baraki Barak lies in a mountainous area in the valley of the Logar River, and the main Ghazni-Kabul road passes about 20 km to its west.
Lunda Norte is a province of Angola with an area of 103,760 km2 and a population of 862,566, bordering the Democratic Republic of Congo to the northeast and Lunda Sul to the south.
After independence, Angola's first President, Agostino Neto, made Lucapa the provincial capital of Lunda Norte, but the capital was later moved to Dundo.

Lunda Norte is rich in gold and diamonds but remains vastly underdeveloped and impoverished; the Cuango River valley, Angola's richest diamond area, is located in the province, and companies such as DeBeers and Endiama mine there, while UNITA used diamond money to fund war efforts.

The Lunda province, whose capital was Saurimo, was created by the Portuguese colonial empire on July 13, 1895, and was divided into Lunda-Sul and Lunda-Norte by a 1978 constitution act of the MPLA government.
Lunda Norte is well known for its sculptures, most notably The Thinker (O Pensador), a sculpture of a man holding his head, and is rich in flora and fauna.
Mount Crescent is a mountain located in the Crescent Range of the White Mountains in Randolph, New Hampshire, with an elevation of 3,251 ft (991 m).
The summit of Mount Crescent is the second highest mountain summit in Randolph, after Black Crescent Mountain (3,264 feet, 995 m), and both mountains are in Randolph's Ice Gulch Town Forest.
On the 1896 topographic map, Mount Crescent is shown as Randolph Mtn. with an elevation of 3,280 ft, while Black Crescent is shown as Mt. Crescent with an elevation of 3,322 ft.
The Crescent Range, sometimes referred to as the Randolph Mountains, is located in the White Mountains of New Hampshire in the United States.
The highest peak in the Crescent Range is Black Crescent Mountain, with an elevation of 3,264 ft.
Crescent Mills (formerly Crescent City and Crescent) is a census-designated place in Plumas County, California, United States, located 3.5 mi southeast of Greenville.
Crescent Mills had a population of 196 at the 2010 census, down from 258 at the 2000 census.
Somanya is a town and the capital of Yilo Krobo District in the Eastern Region of south Ghana, and it is now around 30 miles from Accra, a distance shrinking as Accra expands northwards.

Somanya had a 2013 settlement population of 20,596 people, and the 2010 Population and Housing Census of Ghana put the population of Somanya at 87,847, representing 3.3 of the region's total population.
In Somanya, males constitute 48.2 percent of the population and females 51.8 percent according to the Ghana Census Bureau, and the entire Krobo district is described as rural.
Santa Cruz is a town in the eastern part of the island of Santiago, Cape Verde, located more than 2 kilometres southeast of the municipal seat Santa Cruz Pedra Badejo and over 30 km NNW of Praia.
Santa Cruz had a 2010 population of 2,019 and forms part of the Pedra Badejo area, which had about 20,000 people as of 2010.
Santa Cruz, Cape Verde, is situated on the road linking Praia and Tarrafal through Pedra Badejo, the EN1-ST02.
Black Crescent Mountain is a mountain in the Crescent Range of the White Mountains, 4.4 mi north of Randolph and 4.7 mi southwest of Berlin in New Hampshire.
The summit of Black Crescent Mountain is on the eastern boundary of the White Mountain National Forest.
Orange Walk Town is the fourth largest town in Belize, with a population of about 13,400 according to the 2010 Population and Housing Census, and is the capital of the Orange Walk District.
Orange Walk Town is located on the left bank of the New River, 53 mi north of Belize City and 30 mi south of Corozal Town.

Randolph is a heavily forested town in Coos County, New Hampshire, U.S., extending from the northern slopes of the White Mountains of the Presidential Range to the Crescent Range and Berlin, with U.S. Route 2 cutting through the middle.
The northern and southern parts of Randolph, New Hampshire, lie within the White Mountain National Forest and the Ice Gulch Town Forest, while the central part is the settled portion of the town.
As of the 2010 census, the town of Randolph, New Hampshire, had a total population of 310.
Mount Vernon is a city in and the county seat of Posey County, Indiana, United States, located in the state's far southwestern corner.
Mount Vernon, Indiana, is the westernmost city in the state but not the southernmost, that distinction belonging to Rockport, about 40 miles to the southeast.
Mount Vernon, Indiana, had a population of 6,687 at the 2010 census, is located in Black Township, and is part of the Evansville, Indiana, metropolitan area, which had a 2010 population of 358,676.

Tarrafal de São Nicolau is a town in the western part of the island of São Nicolau, Cape Verde, with a 2010 population of 3,733, and it is the island's most populated place, more populous than the main city Ribeira Brava.
Tarrafal de São Nicolau lies on the west coast, 9 km southwest of Ribeira Brava, is the seat of the Tarrafal de São Nicolau Municipality, and is the main port of the island.

The port of Tarrafal de São Nicolau, expanded before 1990 and completed in 1991, is 137 metres long, fits two boats, and offers ferry services to other islands including São Vicente, Sal and Santiago.

The Apollo spacecraft was composed of three parts designed to accomplish the American Apollo program's goal of landing astronauts on the Moon by the end of the 1960s and returning them safely to Earth.
The expendable Apollo spacecraft consisted of a combined Command/Service Module (CSM) and a Lunar Module (LM).

Two additional components complemented the Apollo spacecraft stack: the Spacecraft Lunar Module Adapter (SLA), which shields the LM from launch stress and connects the CSM to the Saturn launch vehicle, and the Launch Escape System (LES), which carries the crew in the Command Module safely away from the launch vehicle in an emergency.
Moon Machines is a Science Channel HD documentary miniseries of six episodes, shown in the US and UK, documenting the engineering challenges of the Apollo Program to land a man on the Moon.

Moon Machines covers the Saturn V, the Command Module, the Lunar Module, the space suits, the Guidance and Control Computer and the Lunar Rover, and was created by the team who made In the Shadow of the Moon in association with NASA to commemorate its fiftieth anniversary in 2008.
Moon Machines first aired in June 2008 and was released on DVD in June 2009.

Apollo 8, the second human spaceflight mission in the United States Apollo space program, was launched on December 21, 1968, and became the first crewed spacecraft to leave Earth orbit, reach the Moon, orbit it and return safely to Earth.
The Apollo 8 crew was Commander Frank Borman, Command Module Pilot James Lovell and Lunar Module Pilot William Anders.

Apollo 8 was the third flight of the Saturn V rocket and its first crewed launch, and was the first human spaceflight launch from the Kennedy Space Center, Florida, located adjacent to Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
The Apollo 8 crew became the first humans to see Earth as a whole planet, directly see the far side of the Moon with their own eyes, and witness an Earthrise.

Apollo 12 was the sixth manned flight in the United States Apollo program and the second to land on the Moon, an H type mission, launched on November 14, 1969, from the Kennedy Space Center, Florida, four months after Apollo 11.

Apollo 12 commander Charles Pete Conrad and Lunar Module Pilot Alan L. Bean performed just over one day and seven hours of lunar surface activity, while Command Module Pilot Richard F. Gordon remained in lunar orbit.
The Apollo 12 landing site was in the southeastern portion of the Ocean of Storms.
Apollo 16 was the tenth manned mission in the United States Apollo space program, the fifth and penultimate mission to land on the Moon, and the first to land in the lunar highlands.
Apollo 16, the second of the so-called J missions, was crewed by Commander John Young, Lunar Module Pilot Charles Duke and Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly.
Apollo 16 launched from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 12:54 PM EST on April 16, 1972, lasted 11 days, 1 hour and 51 minutes, and concluded at 2:45 PM EST on April 27.
Moon trees are trees grown from 500 seeds taken into orbit around the Moon by Stuart Roosa during the Apollo 14 mission in 1971.

Stuart Roosa, the Command Module Pilot on the Apollo 14 mission and a former smoke jumper, was contacted by Ed Cliff, then Chief of the Forest Service, who proposed the idea of taking the seeds along.
The seeds for the Moon trees experiment were chosen from five tree types: Loblolly Pine, Sycamore, Sweetgum, Redwood and Douglas Fir.

Stuart Allen Stu Roosa (August 16, 1933 - December 12, 1994), a Colonel in the USAF, was an American aeronautical engineer, Air Force pilot, test pilot and NASA astronaut who was the Command Module Pilot for Apollo 14.
The Apollo 14 mission, on which Stuart Roosa flew, lasted from January 31 to February 9, 1971, and was the third mission to land astronauts on the Moon, with Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell.

While Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell spent two days on the lunar surface, Stuart Roosa conducted experiments from orbit in the Command Module Kitty Hawk and was one of only 24 people to travel to the Moon.
AS-201 (or SA-201), flown February 26, 1966, was the first unmanned test flight of an entire production Block I Apollo Command/Service Module and the Saturn IB launch vehicle.
The AS-201 spacecraft consisted of the second Block I command module and the first Block I service module.

The AS-201 suborbital flight was a partially successful demonstration of the service propulsion system and the reaction control systems of both modules, and it successfully demonstrated the Command Module heat shield's ability to survive re-entry from low Earth orbit.
The Lunex Project was a US Air Force 1958 plan for a manned lunar landing prior to the Apollo Program.
The final Lunex expedition plan in 1961 called for a 21-airman underground Air Force base on the Moon by 1968 at a total cost of $7.5 billion.

The Lunex vehicle, composed of a landing module and a lifting body return/re-entry module, would land the entire vehicle and all astronauts on the surface, whereas the final Apollo mission used orbital rendezvous with a separate ascent module.
The original plan for Apollo was direct ascent, similar to Lunex; the primary distinction between the later Apollo missions and the Lunex Project was the orbital rendezvous maneuver.
Apollo 9 was the third manned mission in the United States Apollo space program and the first flight of the Command/Service Module (CSM) with the Lunar Module (LM).
The Apollo 9 crew consisted of Commander James McDivitt, Command Module Pilot David Scott and Lunar Module Pilot Rusty Schweickart.
Apollo 9 spent ten days in low Earth orbit testing the LM engines, backpack life support systems, navigation systems and docking maneuvers, and was the second manned launch of a Saturn V rocket.

Wolverine/Nick Fury: The Scorpio Connection is a 1989 graphic novel published by Marvel Comics, written by Archie Goodwin and drawn by Howard Chaykin, and it is the first part of the Wolverine/Nick Fury trilogy.
In Wolverine/Nick Fury: The Scorpio Connection, a new Scorpio attempts to kill Nick Fury, and Wolverine investigates the murder of a friend who once saved his life at the hands of the new Scorpio.
Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. was a feature in the anthology comic Strange Tales that introduced the fictional spy agency S.H.I.E.L.D. into the Marvel Comics world.

The Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. feature reintroduced Nick Fury as an older character from the WWII comic Sgt. Fury, replaced the Human Torch feature in Strange Tales, and ran alongside the Dr. Strange feature.
After the Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. feature ended, a comic title was published that has had several volumes, as well as a comic strip.
Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D.: Empyre is a forty-eight page novel written by Will Murray and published by Berkley Books and Marvel Comics in 2000.
Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D.: Empyre is the first appearance of the character Nick Fury in novel form, with illustrations by longtime Nick Fury artist Jim Steranko.
The plot of Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D.: Empyre revived the concept of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s psychic sensory division from the old Stan Lee and Jack Kirby comics.
Nick Fury vs. S.H.I.E.L.D. is a six issue comic book miniseries published by Marvel Comics in 1988, written by Bob Harras and drawn by Paul Neary, with each 48-page issue referred to as a book.
Nick Fury vs. S.H.I.E.L.D. was the first time in almost twenty years that Nick Fury and S.H.I.E.L.D. were the main focus of a series, and the miniseries sold exceptionally well.
The success of Nick Fury vs. S.H.I.E.L.D. prompted Marvel to produce an ongoing series, Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D., in 1989, which lasted 47 issues.
Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. is an American television film based on the Marvel Comics character Nick Fury, first broadcast on May 26, 1998 on Fox and directed by Rod Hardy.

In Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D., David Hasselhoff stars as Fury, a retired super spy approached to return to duty to take down the terrorist organization HYDRA, which threatens to attack Manhattan with the Death's Head virus.

In Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D., Lisa Rinna plays Contessa Valentina Val Allegra de Fontaine and Sandra Hess plays Andrea von Strucker / Viper, and the film was released on DVD on September 30, 2008.
Andrea von Strucker and Andreas von Strucker are two fictional characters appearing in American comic books published by Marvel Comics.
Andrea von Strucker and Andreas von Strucker are the German twin children of the supervillain Baron von Strucker of HYDRA and the half-siblings of Werner von Strucker.
Bunduki is a 1975 novel by J. T. Edson and the first work in the Bunduki series that followed.
The Bunduki series by J. T. Edson involves characters related to Tarzan and was initially authorized by the estate of Edgar Rice Burroughs.
In the opening of the 1975 novel Bunduki by J. T. Edson, the main protagonists are transported from Earth to Zillikian.
A set of tiles covers the characters Nick Fury, Nick Fury Jr., Ultimate Nick Fury, or any other alternative version of the character published by Marvel Comics.
Nick Fury Jr. and Ultimate Nick Fury are alternative versions of the Marvel Comics character Nick Fury, and these tiles cover them.
Nick Fury is a 2017 ongoing comic book series published by Marvel Comics, written by James Dale Robinson and primarily drawn by ACO.
The 2017 Nick Fury comic book series was the first series to feature Nick Fury Jr. as its main character.

General Nicholas Joseph Nick Fury is a fictional character in comic books published by Marvel Comics' Ultimate Marvel section, a different version of Nick Fury or Nick Fury Jr., his son and successor as director of S.H.I.E.L.D.

General Nicholas Joseph Nick Fury first appeared in Ultimate Marvel Team-Up and Ultimate X-Men, reappeared regularly in Ultimate Spider-Man, and has a recurring role as general of S.H.I.E.L.D. and leader of the Ultimates, a reimagining of the Avengers.

The Ultimate Marvel version of Nick Fury was designed to look like Samuel L. Jackson, who later went on to portray Nick Fury in several Marvel films and television shows set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
Sitting Pretty is a 1933 American Pre-Code musical comedy film about two aspiring but untalented songwriters, played by Jack Oakie and Jack Haley.

In Sitting Pretty, Ginger Rogers and Thelma Todd join the two songwriters on their trip from New York City to Hollywood to find their fortune; the film was directed by Harry Joe Brown and featured the Pickens Sisters as themselves.
Hello, Everybody! is a 1933 American Pre-Code musical film directed by William A. Seiter and written by Lawrence Hazard, Fannie Hurst and Dorothy Yost.
Hello, Everybody! stars Kate Smith, Randolph Scott, Sally Blane, Charley Grapewin, George Barbier, Wade Boteler and Julia Swayne Gordon, and was released on February 17, 1933, by Paramount Pictures.
College Humor is a 1933 American pre-Code musical comedy film directed by Wesley Ruggles and starring Bing Crosby, Jack Oakie, Richard Arlen, Mary Kornman and Mary Carlisle.

College Humor, released by Paramount Pictures and based on a story by Dean Fales, is about a college professor and the school's star football player who become rivals for the same beautiful coed, and it co-stars George Burns and Gracie Allen.
Girl Without a Room is a 1933 American Pre-Code musical comedy film starring Charles Farrell, Charles Ruggles and Marguerite Churchill.
Girl Without a Room is an early light comedy farce set in Paris, written by Claude Binyon, Frank Butler and Jack Lait and directed by Ralph Murphy.
Going Hollywood is a 1933 American pre-Code musical film directed by Raoul Walsh and starring Marion Davies and Bing Crosby.
Going Hollywood was written by Donald Ogden Stewart, based on a story by Frances Marion, and was released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer on December 22, 1933.

International House is a 1933 American pre-Code comedy film starring Peggy Hopkins Joyce and W. C. Fields, directed by A. Edward Sutherland and released by Paramount Pictures, whose tagline was The Grand Hotel of comedy.

International House mixes comedy and musical acts tied together by a slim plot line, in the style of the Big Broadcast pictures, and provides a snapshot of popular stage and radio acts of the era alongside Burns and Allen.
Melody Cruise is a 1933 American Pre-Code musical romantic comedy film directed by Mark Sandrich.
Melody Cruise, a 1933 American Pre-Code film, is a musical romantic comedy that was directed by Mark Sandrich.
My Lips Betray is a 1933 American Pre-Code musical comedy film directed by John G. Blystone and starring Lilian Harvey, John Boles and El Brendel.
The sets for the 1933 American Pre-Code musical comedy My Lips Betray were designed by the art director Joseph C. Wright.
Hallelujah, I'm a Bum is a 1933 American Pre-Code musical comedy film directed by Lewis Milestone and set in the Great Depression.
Lewis Milestone is the director of the 1933 film Hallelujah, I'm a Bum, which is set in the Great Depression.
Harry Lillis Bing Crosby Jr. (May 3, 1903 - October 14, 1977) was an American singer and actor.

Bing Crosby's trademark warm bass-baritone voice made him the best-selling recording artist of the 20th century, having sold over one billion records, tapes, compact discs and digital downloads around the world.
Binford & Mort Publishing is a book publishing company located in Hillsboro, Oregon, United States, founded in 1930, and previously known as Metropolitan Press and Binfords & Mort.

Binford & Mort Publishing was at one time the largest book publisher in the Pacific Northwest, and is a privately owned company focused on books from the Pacific Northwest, including many titles covering Oregon's history.
David Hamilton Koch (born May 3, 1940) is an American businessman, philanthropist, political activist and chemical engineer.

David Hamilton Koch joined the family business Koch Industries in 1970, became president of the subsidiary Koch Engineering in 1979, and became a co-owner of Koch Industries with his older brother Charles in 1983.
Koch Industries is a conglomerate that is the second-largest privately held company in the United States, and David Hamilton Koch is now an executive vice president there.

David Hamilton Koch, an influential libertarian, was the 1980 Libertarian Party candidate for Vice President of the United States, helped finance that campaign, and founded Citizens for a Sound Economy.
David Hamilton Koch and his brother Charles have donated to political advocacy groups and political campaigns, almost entirely Republican.
